Soybean Harvest Over 80 Percent Complete
Agricultural Summary: Last week was another big week for soybean
harvest as 28 percent of the state's soybeans were harvested. Iowa
farmers harvested 14 percent of the state's corn last week as well, but
others are delaying harvest to allow the corn to dry down in the field.
Other agricultural activities included fall application of dry fertilizer,
manure spreading, and tillage of bean stubble.
There were 6.3 days suitable for fieldwork, compared to 6.7 days
last week, and 5.0 days last year at this time. Topsoil moisture rated
40 percent very short, 37 percent short, 23 percent adequate, and
0 percent surplus across Iowa. Subsoil moisture rated 50 percent
very short, 39 percent short, 11 percent adequate, and 0 percent
surplus.
Field Crops Report: The corn acreage harvested for grain or seed
was 31 percent, ahead of last year's progress of 20 percent but two
days behind the 5-year average of 35 percent harvested. The percent
moisture of field corn was 20 percent, while the percent moisture
of harvested corn was 17 percent. Corn lodging rated 56 percent
none, 30 percent light, 12 percent moderate, and 2 percent heavy.
Corn ear droppage rated 62 percent none, 30 percent light,

Corn Harvest Commences
Agricultural Summary: With rain falling across much of the state late
last week, crop and pasture conditions improved slightly; however,
the rain may have arrived too late to help the corn and most
soybeans. Later planted soybeans and pastures may benefit from the
rains, but it appears to be a rain situation where Iowa received "too
little, too late." Field activity last week included finishing silage
harvest, final cutting of hay, and harvesting corn for grain. Winter
hay supplies and silage continued to be fed as supplemental feed to
livestock.
There were 5.1 days suitable for fieldwork, compared to 6.9 days
last week and 6.5 days last year at this time. Topsoil moisture rated

surplus.

Alfalfa Third Cutting at 80 Percent Completion
Agricultural Summary: Widespread hot and dry weather hastened corn
maturity across Iowa and soybeans dropped leaves prematurely. Corn
ears were dropping and harvest for silage began two to three weeks
earlier than normal. There were scattered reports of corn being harvested
in southern Iowa. Supplemental feeding of hay continued, and baling
and grazing of CRP was an option for some producers.
There were 6.7 days suitable for fieldwork, compared to 6.8 days last
week and 5.8 days last year at this time. Topsoil moisture rated
60 percent very short, 34 percent short, 6 percent adequate, and 0 percent
surplus across Iowa. Subsoil moisture rated 48 percent very short,
40 percent short, 12 percent adequate, and 0 percent surplus.
Field Crops Report: The corn acreage in or past dough stage was
88 percent, behind last year's progress of 94 percent and two days behind
the 5-year average of 91 percent dough stage. The corn acreage in or
past dent stage was 61 percent, behind last year's progress of 70 percent
and two days behind the 5-year average of 69 percent dent stage. The
corn acreage in mature stage was 10 percent, slightly behind last year's
progress of 12 percent and two days behind the 5-year average of
20 percent poor, 36 percent fair, 33 percent good, and 3 percent
excellent. The soybean acreage with leaves turning color was
15 percent, behind last year's progress of 20 percent and similar to the
5-year average of 16 percent leaves turning color. The soybean acreage
dropping leaves was 4 percent, slightly ahead of last year's progress of
3 percent and the 5-year average of 2 percent dropping leaves. Soybean
condition rated 9 percent very poor, 23 percent poor, 38 percent fair,
27 percent good, and 3 percent excellent. The third cutting of alfalfa
hay was 80 percent complete, ahead of last year's progress of 70 percent
complete and seven days ahead of the 5-year average of 67 percent
complete. Hay condition rated 26 percent very poor, 32 percent poor,
29 percent fair, 12 percent good, and 1 percent excellent.
Livestock, Pasture, and Range Report: Cattle gains slowed, and calves
were weaned early due to hot and dry conditions and favorable cattle
prices. Pasture and range condition rated 47 percent very poor,
34 percent poor, 16 percent fair, 3 percent good, and 0 percent excellent.

were showing the most stress. Aphid levels in soybeans were high
enough to spray in many fields. Pastures were reported as
deteriorating quickly, and supplemental feeding of hay continued.
There was a common request for rain throughout the state.

2004 Harvest Just About Wrapped Up
Agricultural Summary: Corn harvest in Iowa was nearly complete except
for scattered fields. Producers were concentrating on fall tillage and
fertilization application. For the northern two-thirds of the state, frozen
or muddy soil conditions and shortened days contributed to slower
activity. Some farmers are beginning to put machinery away for the
winter. Elevators were trying to move grain from piles on the ground to
inside storage. Some elevators were accepting corn at limited times
depending on rail car availability. Reporters noted tile and terrace work
was underway and manure was being applied.
There were 4.1 days suitable for fieldwork in Iowa. Topsoil moisture
rated 2 percent very short, 8 percent short, 75 percent adequate, and
15 percent surplus. Subsoil moisture rated 6 percent very short,
20 percent short, 65 percent adequate, and 9 percent surplus.
Field Crops Report: The corn acreage harvested for grain or seed
reached 97 percent. Fall fertilizer application in preparation for the
farm to elevator was rated 30 percent none, 35 percent light, 25 percent
moderate, and 10 percent heavy. Off-farm grain storage availability
rated 64 percent short, 35 percent adequate, and 1 percent surplus. On-
farm grain storage availability rated 65 percent short, and 33 percent
adequate, and 2 percent surplus. Hay and roughage availability rated
6 percent short, 76 percent adequate, and 18 percent surplus. Quality of
hay and roughage supplies rated 6 percent poor, 37 percent fair, and
34 percent none, 24 percent light, 27 percent moderate, and 15 percent
heavy.

Soybean Harvest Picking Up Speed
Agricultural Summary: The lower two-thirds of the state experienced a
good drying week for crops. Soybean harvest is progressing rapidly in
these areas, while producers in the northernmost section of Iowa
indicated heavy rains slowed harvest. Rain helped green up pastures, but
slowed silage chopping. Reporters note soybean maturity varies widely
from green to harvest. There were scattered reports of white mold in
soybeans with some fields much worse than others. Producers in the
southern section of the state would like to see some moisture and there
were reports of some ponds being built.
There were 5.3 days suitable for fieldwork this week in Iowa. Topsoil
moisture rated 7 percent very short, 24 percent short, 59 percent
adequate, and 10 percent surplus. Subsoil moisture rated 7 percent very
short, 22 percent short, 63 percent adequate, and 8 percent surplus.

97 percent, slightly behind both last year's and the 5-year average of

the 5-year average of 87 percent. The corn harvested for grain or seed
was 5 percent, 5 days behind last year's 9 percent harvest at this time and
8 days behind the 5-year average of 11 percent. The average percent
moisture of all field corn was 30 percent, while the average percent
moisture of harvested field corn was 26 percent. Corn lodging rated
62 percent none, 26 percent light, 9 percent moderate, and 3 percent
heavy. Corn ear droppage rated 72 percent none, 25 percent light, and
